journey:jesus-mafa.a: Mafa Christian community, with the French priest François Vidil and French artists
journey:jesus-mafa.l: Widely reproduced; images held in the Vanderbilt Divinity Library's Art in the Christian Tradition collection and elsewhere
journey:jesus-mafa.m: Series of paintings based on photographs of staged Gospel scenes
journey:jesus-mafa.noimg: © JESUS MAFA (Vie de Jésus Mafa). View the series in the Vanderbilt Divinity Library's Art in the Christian Tradition database.

x.summary: The Jesus Mafa images grew out of a project with Christians of the Mafa people of northern Cameroon. Villagers acted out Gospel stories in their own setting, the scenes were photographed, and artists then painted them, showing Jesus, Mary and the disciples as Mafa men and women in a West African landscape. The result is a set of luminous, dignified scenes from Christ's life that have become well known in churches across Africa, Europe and the Americas.
facts: The scenes follow Gospel readings in the church's lectionary, including the Nativity, the Last Supper and the Resurrection.
The project's aim was to make the Gospel visible in local African forms instead of through imported European images.
The project was led by the French Catholic priest François Vidil; in the United States the prints were long distributed by the Josephites, a society of priests serving African American Catholics.
